title: i-Ready: 13 Million Students, Zero Meaningful Evidence
author: Unknown
summary: The Digital Delusion examines 15 years of research on i-Ready, used by 13 million K-8 students in the US, and finds zero randomized controlled trials and zero top-tier peer-reviewed studies demonstrating its effectiveness. The two Johns Hopkins studies—funded by Curriculum Associates (i-Ready's developer)—found no statistically significant impact on reading and only a clinically meaningless 0.8% improvement in math across 7,646 students. The article argues that i-Ready fundamentally misunderstands formative assessment: effective formative assessment works because it informs the teacher's instruction, not because of immediate student feedback. When i-Ready algorithms make all instructional decisions, teachers lose the critical information needed to adapt teaching, removing the mechanism that makes formative assessment effective.
points: After 15 years and 13 million students, i-Ready has zero rigorous independent research supporting effectiveness—no randomized controlled trials, no top-tier peer-reviewed studies, only lower-tier and gray literature.

The Johns Hopkins studies (non-peer-reviewed white papers) found no significant impact on reading achievement and only a 0.8% improvement in math, which is clinically meaningless despite statistical significance.
i-Ready misunderstands how formative assessment works: the power lies in the information it provides to teachers to adjust instruction, not in immediate feedback to students.

When an adaptive system controls all instructional decisions, teachers cannot see misconceptions as they emerge and cannot adjust teaching in real time—the key mechanism of formative assessment is removed.
The absence of rigorous evidence for a tool affecting one-third of US elementary students signals a broader failure in how educational technology is evaluated and adopted.
quotes: Fifteen years. Thirteen million students. Not a single high-quality, independent study showing i-Ready improves learning.

On reading, the researchers concluded: 'Results of this study did not show any statistically significant associations between i-Ready Personalized Instruction usage and SBA ELA achievement.' In plain terms, they found no measurable impact.

In medicine, we distinguish between statistical significance and clinical significance. The former tells us that a result is unlikely to be due to chance; the latter asks whether that result is actually meaningful for patients.
Formative assessment is only 'formative' when the information it generates changes what the teacher does in response.

When students use i-Ready, the system determines which questions are asked, what feedback is given, and how instruction is sequenced. The only thing teachers see are summary performance metrics. They don't see the questions, the responses, or the misconceptions as they emerge.” Archived from The Digital Delusion on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
